# Counterfact

Counterfact turns an OpenAPI or Swagger document into a live, stateful,
programmable TypeScript mock server. It generates typed route handlers and
request/response types, supports hot reload, and can be used from the CLI or
as a library. Requires Node.js 22 or newer.

This file is an index. Read the smallest relevant document before generating
Counterfact code, and use the generated `types/` files in the user's project
as the authoritative source for endpoint-specific types.

## Start here

- `README.md` — short overview, installation, and the main workflow.
- `docs/first-10-minutes.md` — recommended end-to-end workflow, including
  generated files, state, deterministic tests, and bounded agent tasks.
- `docs/getting-started.md` — step-by-step CLI tutorial and lifecycle guidance.

## When generating route handlers

- `docs/reference.md` — canonical reference for generated file structure, route
  handlers, the `$` parameter, response builders, state, hot reload, and CLI
  options.
- `docs/features/routes.md` — practical route-handler examples, request data,
  response content, cookies, auth, latency, and streaming.
- `docs/features/generated-code.md` — what belongs in `routes/` versus
  generated `types/`, including versioned APIs.
- `docs/features/state.md` — context objects, nested contexts, JSON data, and
  sharing state across API groups.
- `docs/features/middleware.md` — custom Koa middleware.

Before writing a handler, inspect the user's generated type import and the
operation's `HTTP_*` type. Do not invent request or response fields from the
OpenAPI document when the generated TypeScript types are available. Do not
edit generated files under `types/`; edit files under `routes/`.

## When using Counterfact as a library

- `docs/features/programmatic-api.md` — `counterfact()` configuration,
  lifecycle, context access, stores, multiple specs, and test integration.
- `docs/reference.md` — programmatic API and multi-version reference details.

## When choosing a workflow or pattern

- `docs/usage.md` — feature map and links to the documentation.
- `docs/patterns/ai-assisted-implementation.md` — implementing handlers with
  an AI coding assistant.
- `docs/patterns/agentic-sandbox.md` — using Counterfact as a bounded API
  sandbox for an agent.
- `docs/patterns/automated-integration-tests.md` — real HTTP test setup.
- `docs/patterns/hybrid-proxy.md` — combining mocked and upstream routes.
- `docs/patterns/simulate-failures.md` — deterministic error behavior.
- `docs/patterns/simulate-latency.md` — deterministic latency behavior.
- `docs/patterns/scenario-scripts.md` — pre-seeding and orchestrating state.

## Troubleshooting and boundaries

- `docs/faq.md` — answers about state, validation, type safety, regeneration,
  and programmatic use.
- `docs/comparison.md` — differences from other mock-server tools.

Counterfact executes TypeScript route files but does not type-check the user's
project. The user should run their normal TypeScript check. Regeneration can
rewrite generated types and may add route scaffolding; preserve user-authored
handler bodies and avoid destructive generation flags unless explicitly asked.

## Package and source references

- `package.json` — package entry point, CLI binary, supported Node version, and
  published files.
- `dist/server/types.d.ts` — package-level TypeScript declarations exposed by
  the library entry point after installation.
- `https://counterfact.dev` — rendered online documentation.
- `https://github.com/counterfact/example-petstore` — complete example project.
